# Same-source post-arrival cleanup-only V1

This narrowly selected V9 controller addresses source49c3's verified staging arrival after the operator was interrupted with no observed terminal exit. It neither extends the installation grant nor permits installation, source writes, service restart, roles, database writes, deployment, publication or production. The original operator exit remains unknown, never relabelled PASS or exit1. A new independent fifteen-minute certificate permits exact dead-lock custody and only the unchanged Python engine's removal of retained installation `next` and consumed `packet`. The live compiled tree is never selected for deletion.

The release owner must independently review this controller and pass the whole `test/cleanup-only-recovery-controls.test.ts` through the existing focused hosted diagnostic route. That diagnostic is operational controller evidence, not new application CI, compiler, staging arrival or browser acceptance. The unchanged original source's successful full CI/build/consumer evidence remains tied to its original source and runs.

The operator verifies every remote file hash before use. Root alone owns transfer and the actual lease.

The private config contains `frozen` (the clean original source checkout), `controller` (the reviewed new tool commit), `remoteToolDirectory`, `remoteReconciliation`, `reconciliationPath`, `reconciliationSha256`, `attemptName` (`cleanup-only-v1-...`), `out` (a NEW directory), `originalEvidence`, `interruptionPath`, `originalOutputDirectory`, and, for custody/cleanup, `certificatePath`, `remoteCertificate`, `humanEvidencePath`. No original authority/consumption/result may exist. Include every prior failed attempt and its complete inventory; never overwrite old observations.

## Preserved controls and limits

No original guard, installer, Python engine, workflow, package, SQL, provider binding or application test is changed. Full audits are read-only metadata and byte verification, not application tests or builds. The read-only runtime lift intentionally uses the expired grant only for immutable build/origin comparison; its permission callback validates the new cleanup certificate and active lease. It can never activate/install. The actual root must confirm source/CI witness policy freshness and shared queue/lease authority before invoking this operator. If current policy cannot admit a new cleanup-only purpose, stop for the actual policy decision rather than misusing the expired installation grant.
